title: Hazard Pointer Poisoning Avoidance Failure
pattern: Reading a node pointer, registering it as a hazard pointer, and then traversing to its successor without verifying that the node is still valid.
why_bad: A concurrent updater could remove and free the node in the split-second gap *before* the hazard pointer was registered. If this occurs, the traversal pointer `curr` becomes invalid, and accessing `curr->next` results in memory corruption.
detection: A hazard-pointer registration block that does not re-read the active head/parent pointer to verify the node is still linked in the data structure.
counterexample: Verifying the node is still live after registering the hazard pointer.
